issues.description: Inconsistent fixed-point type width controlled by the FIX_LEN macro across repository artifacts. In the template's tests header (tests/src/math_fix.h) FIX_LEN is defined as 4 (making fix_t a 32-bit type), while the template's example program source (example_program/src/math_fix.c) defines FIX_LEN as 8 (making fix_t a 64-bit type). The solution repository's tests use FIX_LEN = 8. Because FIX_LEN determines the underlying typedef for fix_t, these conflicting definitions cause different translation units to compile with different fix_t sizes, producing ABI/type mismatches, incorrect arithmetic results, and likely test or runtime failures for students.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make FIX_LEN consistent across the repository. Recommended options:
1) Change the template tests header (tests/src/math_fix.h) to #define FIX_LEN 8 to match the example program and the solution, so fix_t is 64-bit everywhere.
OR
2) Centralize the FIX_LEN definition in a single header (e.g. example_program/src/math_fix.h or a common header) and include it from all compilation units (tests and example_program) so all translation units use the same FIX_LEN. Update documentation/comments to state the intended FIX_LEN value for the exercise.
